question: Is speaker identity present in this audio for a cheap spectral front-end?
feature: 20-band log LTAS, 25ms/10ms, 100-4000 Hz, L2-normalised, cosine similarity
cost: numpy only; 4x90s WAV already in tree; no model, no network, no GPU
note_on_overlap: empty by construction: AMI audible turns tile (0.0% overlap, TWO-SPEAKER-TURNS.md) -- not measured here

meta.overlap_slice_status: empty by construction: AMI audible turns tile (0.0% overlap, TWO-SPEAKER-TURNS.md) -- not measured here

results.slice: farfield: single mic, same 90 s window

verdict: NEGATIVE: a trivial magnitude-only spectral statistic fails even on CLEAN single-speaker audio. This probe cannot support the architecture question. A learned embedding may still work, but nothing here licenses the claim that a cheap spectral front-end can carry speaker identity.

positive_control.what: F0 separates the two voice classes (MEE vs FEO) in this same harness
positive_control.verdict: harness is sound: it resolves a signal known to be present

interpretation_caveat: Both AUCs land BELOW 0.5, i.e. inverted rather than merely flat. An inverted result is a harness signature -- exactly the shape of the 0.289 overlap inversion already caught in TWO-SPEAKER-TURNS.md. Duration control (AUC gets MORE inverted as segments get longer, 0.33 -> 0.13) and temporal-drift control (corr(cos,|dt|) = -0.05) did not explain it, and the F0 positive control proves the code path resolves a real signal. The defensible reading is therefore the WEAK one: a magnitude-only log-spectrogram statistic does not carry usable speaker identity in this corpus. The inversion itself is NOT claimed as a result -- it is flagged as unexplained.
